topic_detail: Argues that the schooling system and the army are programming given by the state: people are conscripted right after high school because it is easiest then, school was built to train people for factory work, and 'we are still in an industrial-age assembly line'.
audience: young Israelis, parents and aspiring entrepreneurs critical of the education system and army service
caption_vs_video_note: Caption 'התכנות שנותנים לנו מגיל צעיר על ידי הסביבה והמדינה' (the programming we get from a young age from society and the state) fits the video. The cover is a designed title 'השפעת המדינה עלינו' with Matan on stage holding a microphone, a different image from the video.

story.setup: Why soldiers are drafted right after high school.
story.stakes: Whether state institutions shape people into obedient workers.
story.progression: Because at any other age people would not agree to serve (3.4 s); 'I am not against drafting, I was in the special unit 4.5 years, but now I see it differently' (9-17 s); brainwashing by school, home, army, state, politics, most of it irrelevant (17-26 s); the state wants workers not business owners (30-40 s); the education system was set up in the industrial revolution for the assembly line (40-55 s); the problem is we no longer work on one (55-62 s).
story.payoff: The closing line connects schooling to the industrial revolution and the assembly line.
friction_points: t=7 to 17s: personal history of his army service delays the main thesis (interpretation)
t=24 to 35s: a politically charged claim with little evidence (interpretation)
comments object that the army claim is historical or factually off
